package_info.package_manager: N/A (custom Linux malware, not a package manager ecosystem)
package_info.why_malicious: The malware exploits 30 vulnerabilities in outdated WordPress plugins and themes to inject malicious JavaScript into websites, enabling remote command execution and persistent compromise of WordPress-based sites.

execution_context.file_location: Injected into WordPress PHP files or loaded as a malicious binary on the server

malicious_snippets.code_language: python (pseudocode, actual malware likely C/C++ or shell)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the malware scans for outdated WordPress plugins/themes, exploits known vulnerabilities, and injects a malicious JavaScript payload into website files, resulting in persistent client-side compromise and enabling remote command execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Automated exploitation of multiple plugin/theme vulnerabilities and injection of remote JavaScript is highly indicative of mass website compromise.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal WordPress operation does not involve arbitrary code scanning for vulnerabilities or injecting external JavaScript into site files.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated patch management tools may scan for outdated plugins, but do not inject code.

execution_context.file_location: Injected JavaScript within WordPress site pages

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At page load, the injected JavaScript is fetched from a remote attacker-controlled domain and executed in the context of site visitors, enabling credential theft, drive-by downloads, or further exploitation.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Loading JavaScript from an untrusted, external domain is a classic sign of web compromise.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate WordPress sites should not load scripts from unknown or suspicious domains.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Loading scripts from trusted CDNs is common, but not from attacker infrastructure.

attack_chain.action: Malware scans the Linux host for outdated WordPress plugins and themes.
Exploits up to 30 known vulnerabilities to gain write access to WordPress files.
Injects malicious JavaScript into WordPress site files.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of malicious JavaScript in visitors' browsers

attack_chain.action: Injected JavaScript loads additional payloads from attacker-controlled domains when users visit the compromised site.
attack_chain.leads_to: Client-side compromise, credential theft, or further malware delivery

behavioral_signatures: Automated scanning for outdated WordPress plugins/themes
Mass injection of external JavaScript into WordPress PHP or HTML files
Network connections to attacker-controlled domains for script delivery
file_indicators: Unexpected <script src> tags in WordPress theme/plugin files
Modified timestamps on WordPress PHP files
Presence of unfamiliar JavaScript files in webroot
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests to known malicious domains
Unusual traffic from web server to external IPs not associated with legitimate CDNs
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor WordPress site files for unauthorized modifications, especially new or altered <script> tags referencing external domains. Use file integrity monitoring to detect changes in plugin/theme files. Analyze web server logs for outbound requests to suspicious domains. Employ vulnerability management to identify and patch outdated plugins/themes.
